note: Majority: Age of Majority Act, Cap. 226 of the Laws of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines (Act No. 13 of 1987, in force 15 September 1987, revised edition 2009), section 2(1): from that date a person attains full age at eighteen instead of twenty-one. Emancipation by marriage isn't held. Work: Employment of Women, Young Persons and Children Act, Cap. 209 (20/1935, in force 1 July 1938, amended to 53/1992; revised edition 2009), section 2: a child is a person under fourteen and a young person one under eighteen who is no longer a child; section 8(1): a child shall not be employed, save work allowed by Part I (none in industrial undertakings or on ships), light agricultural work for the parent outside school hours, and taking part without fee or reward in an entertainment whose proceeds go to a charitable or educational purpose. Performers: paid performing falls under the ban, so barred under fourteen (my reading of section 8(2)(c)). The Act was read in the copy the University of the West Indies Cave Hill Faculty of Law Library keeps in its UNICEF Children's Law Database (a reproduction of the revised edition, held here as a secondary source because the official law site laws.gov.vc refused this client behind a Cloudflare check). Later labour legislation wasn't looked for. Service: no defence law was read; null.

sources.title: UWI Cave Hill Law Library, UNICEF Children's Law Database: Age of Majority Act, Cap. 226 (Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, revised edition)
sources.said: As from the 15th September, 1987, a person shall attain full age on attaining the age of eighteen instead of attaining the age of twenty-one

sources.said: "child" means a person under the age of fourteen; ... Subject to subsection (2), a child shall not be employed. ... to the participation of a child, without fee or reward, in an entertainment the net proceeds of which are devoted to any charitable or educational purpose
